messages:
sasha (sec): Heads-up — PrivVault rotated the signing key last night and our cosign pipeline failed for a small subset of base-image builds. Not urgent but needs coordinated action.

rahul (infra): saw the alerts early morning, filed a ticket (INC-4721). Some CI jobs retried successfully after we re-exported the old pubkey to the registry.

marta (runtime): thanks. Can you paste the exact error? was it a verification mismatch or an auth failure?

eli (oncall): error in the build logs: `cosign: signature verification failed: no matching key found` + `401 registry push` in one case. Mixed symptoms.

rahul (infra): two distinct failures: 1) cosign verify mismatch for signed layers built before rotation, 2) a short-lived push auth failure for the staging runner while keystore propagation was in flight.

sasha (sec): proposal: schedule a 90-min maintenance window to re-sign the affected base-image batch with the new PrivVault key and rotate the registry signing keychain. We'll need runtime to accept pinned signatures and infra to coordinate RBAC for the re-sign job.

marta (runtime): ok but we need to update the image-allowlist verifier to accept both signer IDs during the handoff. Current verifier only accepts a single key thumbprint. Is dual-thumbprint support possible?

rahul (infra): yes, we can ship a small config toggle to the verifier service: add `signer.accept = ["old-thumb","new-thumb"]` for the window. We'll gate by a feature flag and revert afterwards. Need sec sign-off and a rollout plan.

sasha (sec): approved, but two constraints: (a) audit logs for any re-sign events must be persisted to the auditpipe with 1y retention AND immutable export to our S3 archival bucket, (b) RBAC change must be scoped to the `sig-rekey` job service account only (no wildcard grants).

eli (oncall): adding a quick rollback playbook here: 
```
# rollback: if verifier reports signature mismatch after changes
kubectl set env deployment/verifier FEATURES_ACCEPT_MULTIPLE=false -n security
kubectl rollout restart deployment/verifier -n security
# revoke temporary service account perms
gcloud iam service-accounts remove-iam-policy-binding sig-rekey-sa@prod --role=roles/storage.objectAdmin
```

marta (runtime): noted. I'll prepare the verifier change in a PR with feature-flag + canary (10% of verifier pods). We'll also add a telemetry tag `sig_handoff=true` for any request that uses dual-thumbprint acceptance.

rahul (infra): infra tasks: (1) create the `sig-rekey-sa` with minimal roles, (2) bootstrap the re-sign k8s job with node selectors for builders, (3) ensure cosign binary on builder images is the pinned version 2.0.3 (behavioral change in 2.x caused the mismatch).

sasha (sec): good catch on cosign version — if we re-sign with 2.0.3 but runtime verifier still on older library we'll get drift. Add a preflight: `cosign version` check in the job and `cosign verify` sample against a known-signed artifact.

eli (oncall): audit checklist from ops-bot: 
- created INC:4721
- created PR: github.com/redwood-infra/sig-handoff/pull/12
- scheduled maint: 2026-04-08T01:00:00Z (90m)
- backup: export manifest list for affected images to s3://redwood-image-backups/privvault-rekey/

sasha (sec): also need to update our incident ticket with a scoped timeline and email security-cc list. I'll own the comms. One more ask: can we run a vulnerability quick-scan post re-sign to ensure layer metadata unchanged?

marta (runtime): yes. We'll run trivy in parallel on a sample set and surface any layer ID changes. If hashes change unexpectedly, abort.

rahul (infra): deploying RBAC + job now to staging. I'll post the job manifest and cosign preflight log snippet once done.

ops-bot: job `sig-rekey-staging` started by rahul at 1762345025, status: running.

sasha (sec): perfect — keep this thread for status updates only. If anything blocks, tag me and eli. :white_check_mark:
